hypothesis: The seven distinct valid tiled variants show the 16-row 32x4 shape as the fastest recorded sample, while nearby 8-, 32-row and alternative launch shapes were slower. A contrasting 64-row, 32x16 block keeps X contiguous and four outputs per thread while reducing Y blocks and repeated halo loads per output. Its larger shared tile and 512-thread CTA may offset those savings, so no speedup is assumed.
notes: The new tile loads rows q=-4 through 67 cooperatively; it adds 63 only for q<0 and subtracts 63 only for q>63, preserving q=63 and independently loading both endpoint planes. The launch covers every fixed 64x64x64 output. Inputs and scratch behavior are unchanged. No local oracle or timing was run; controller validation on signed varying inputs and repeated official baseline comparisons are still needed.
transformations: Replace the one-output-per-thread Y derivative with a 64-row shared-memory tile and 32 contiguous X lanes.
Use a 32x16 block to cooperatively initialize all 72 tile rows, including explicit period-63 halos, then compute four Y outputs per thread after one barrier.
Launch one Y tile per plane with the existing 64x64x64 dimensions; retain the stencil expression, full output writes, inputs, and scratch behavior.
